# <span style="color: #171c54;">Accounting, Analysis and Governance in Complex Deals</span>

Last Update: `r format(Sys.Date(), "%B %d")`


::: {.container}
::: {.card}
## Course Description

[Osiris/Sqill](https://eur.sqill.it/reports/163f2c25-9c25-41e4-bd81-8c1b9c3d667c){target="_blank"} contains important information on *Accounting, Analysis and Governance in Complex Deals* (BMME303). Please read all information carefully! Here's a sneak preview of the course description:

This course integrates accounting, financial analysis, and governance, providing students with advanced skills in understanding, assessing, and executing a variety of different transaction types, such as M&A, reorganizations, and other complex deals. Since such transactions often substantially transform businesses, understanding how to analyze and navigate these disruptions is essential for any professional involved in them.
:::

::: {.card}
## Learning Objectives 
- Understand how (financial) information creates and resolves conflicts between business leaders, oversight bodies, and other stakeholders throughout transactions.

- Critically assess complex multi-type and multi-source information in transaction-related valuations and decisions.

- Analyze the complex regulatory environment, including disclosure mandates, surrounding a variety of transaction types.

- Apply regulatory risk assessment frameworks, including commercial and tax due diligence, to transactions.

- Reflect on competencies in accounting, analysis, and governance acquired in other courses throughout the MSc programme to navigate complex deals.
:::



::: {.card}

:::

## Instructional Methods 

The course consists of **11 sessions** that combine elements of workshops and lectures. 

I expect interactive discussions to form the basis of our sessions, requiring students to be prepared, to reflect on previous input, and to actively engage with each other. Therefore, no livestreams or recordings are offered.

- "80% Element" &rarr; Final Exam (closed book) using Chromebook and Ans software

- "20% Element" &rarr; Assignments (think of weekly quizzes, open questions, and other deliverables, such as case solutions) throughout the course (may include peer feedback)

::: {.card}
## GameStop's Push to Acquire eBay

- On May 4, Gamestop's CEO, Ryan Cohen, expressed interest in acquiring eBay: a move that surprised many given the companies' different business models and market positions

- The next day, he gave an interview to CNBC which earned him the headline ***"GameStop’s Ryan Cohen is either the new Buffett or the anti-Buffett"*** [FT](https://www.ft.com/content/a18c4115-7178-456c-a7ff-4b0e7f9ec9aa?syn-25a6b1a6=1){target="_blank"}  

- eBay rejected the bid, calling the offer *"neither credible nor attractive"* [NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/12/business/ebay-gamestop-takeover.html?nl=dealbook&segment_id=219724){target="_blank"} & [8K Filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065088/000155278126000322/e26249_ebay-8k.htm){target="_blank"} & [eBay Letter](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065088/000155278126000322/e26249_ex99-2.htm){target="_blank"}

$\Rightarrow$ Watch the video on [Youtube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bmj2PaxX24E){target="_blank"}!  

$\Rightarrow$ This (short-lived) bid is a great example for accounting, analysis, and governance in complex deals, and we will refer to it throughout the course. Familiarize yourself with the case!

::::

::: {.card}
## Target Selection  

- Translate acquisition **strategy** into practical **target-screening** criteria 

- Connect **value-creating archetypes** to measurable financial indicators

- Discuss **information asymmetry** and governance risks in early target selection

- The **OpenAI-Windsurf** case is used as a stylized application of the screening framework

- **Slides Target Selection** in [HTML](/courses/54132/files/target_identification.html){target="_blank"} and [PDF](/courses/54132/files/target_identification.pdf){target="_blank"} 

- **Key References** beyond text books: @dessaint2017employment, @chen2018financial, @cai2016common (corporate governance and acquisition activity/synergies)

:::


::: {.card}

## Cross Border Issues  

- Connect foreign market entry **motives** and strategy choices to practical deal execution challenges

- Discuss failure risk in cross-border integration, using **Daimler-Chrysler** as a stylized case

- Apply **interest rate parity** to convert foreign target cash flows 

- Evaluate **policy uncertainty** and tariffs as external drivers of cross-border deals

- **Slides Cross Border Issues** in [HTML](/courses/54132/files/cross_border_issues.html){target="_blank"} and [PDF](/courses/54132/files/cross_border_issues.pdf){target="_blank"} 

- **Key References** beyond text books: 
  - @ErelNBERw30597 (cross-border M&A motives)
  - @bonaime2018does (policy uncertainty and M&A activity)
  - @seru2014firm (innovation consequences in merger contexts)
  - @baker2016measuring (measurement of economic policy uncertainty)

:::


::: {.card}

## Valuation and Pricing  

- Understand how boards use fairness opinions to support **fiduciary duties**

- Assess limitations and potential **biases in fairness opinion** design and interpretation

- Reconcile fundamental and relative valuation approaches, and understand when they **converge**

- Evaluate valuation sensitivity to risk, profitability, growth assumptions, and accounting choices

- Distinguish and apply **equity-side and enterprise-side valuation multiples** in deal analysis

- **Slides Fairness Opinions** in [HTML](/courses/54132/files/fairnessopinion.html){target="_blank"} and [PDF](/courses/54132/files/fairnessopinion.pdf){target="_blank"} 

- **Slides Measuring Value** in [HTML](/courses/54132/files/value_measure.html){target="_blank"} and [PDF](/courses/54132/files/value_measure.pdf){target="_blank"} 

- **Guest Lecture** by Marc Goedhart from McKinsey & Company on measuring **value of high-growth companies** (Week Three S1) 

- **Key References**: 
  
  - Fairness Opinions: 
    - @imperatore2024litigation (litigation risk and strategic target valuation in fairness opinions)

  - Measuring Value:  
    - @depamphilis2021mergers (Chapter 8: valuation and pricing in M&amp;A)
    - @koller2010valuation (several chapters on valuation framework, multiples, and value drivers)
    - @shaffer2024multiples (conceptual scheme and interpretation of multiples)


:::


::: {.card}

## Paying and Financing an Acquisition  

- **Payment:** compare cash, stock, and mixed consideration, including **share exchange ratios**, dilution, **collars**, and EPS implications

- **Financing:** evaluate internal funds, debt, seller financing, and sponsor-led buyout structures, including **private equity** and **leveraged buyouts**

- Connect payment and financing choices to risk sharing between bidder and target shareholders

- **Slides Payment** in [HTML](/courses/54132/files/payment.html){target="_blank"} and [PDF](/courses/54132/files/payment.pdf){target="_blank"} 

- **Slides Financing** in [HTML](/courses/54132/files/finance.html){target="_blank"} and [PDF](/courses/54132/files/finance.pdf){target="_blank"} 


- **Key References:** @depamphilis2021mergers (Chapters 11 and 13) and @koller2010valuation (Chapter 31)


:::

::: {.card}

## Due Diligence  

- <strong>Transaction risk assessment:</strong> understand how due diligence reduces information asymmetries 

  - <strong>Tax due diligence:</strong> identify historical and future tax exposures and contractual protection mechanisms 

  - <strong>Financial due diligence:</strong> evaluate EBITDA adjustments when assessing the quality of earnings 

- Translate findings into implications for pricing, structure, negotiation, and final deal recommendations 

- **Slides Due Diligence** in [HTML](/courses/54132/files/due_diligence.html){target="_blank"} and [PDF](/courses/54132/files/due_diligence.pdf){target="_blank"} 


:::


::: {.card}

## Antitrust Issues  

- Analyze existing **antitrust frameworks** across jurisdictions 

- Evaluate how complex deals trigger antitrust concerns and **review** 

- Compare reasoning used in **antitrust debates overt time** 

- Develop **evidence-based case arguments** with clear implications for corporate decision-making

- **Key References** include two Harvard Business School cases:  

  - **Redefining Antitrust in the Age of Big Tech** (324018-PDF-ENG)
  
  - **Bayer-Monsanto: The Challenges of a Mega Merger** (W17764-PDF-ENG)


:::



::: {.card}

## Post-Merger Integration  

- **Purchase Price Allocation** in Business Combinations (ASC 805)

- **Goodwill and Intangible Asset Accounting** 

- **Consolidation Mechanics** including deferred taxes 

- **Accounting Distortions in Market-Based Valuation** and implications for the diversification discount 

- **Practice Case: e.l.f. Beauty acquisition of rhode** ($896.5M + earnout) as a stylized example spanning purchase price allocation, goodwill recognition, impairment testing, and valuation-multiple distortion

- **Key References** include recent filings at SEC and guidance from professional service firms:
  - e.l.f. Beauty 
    - [8-K Announcment](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1600033/000160003325000013/elf-20250528.htm){target="_blank"} 
    - [8-K Closing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1600033/000160003325000037/elf-20250806.htm){target="_blank"} 
    - [10-Q with preliminary PPA](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1600033/000160003325000058/elf-20250930.htm){target="_blank"} 
    - [10-K 2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1600033/000160003326000020/elf-20260331.htm){target="_blank"}
  - [Deloitte: Accounting for Business Combinations under US GAAP](https://dart.deloitte.com/USDART/home/codification/broad-transactions/asc805-10/roadmap-business-combinations/chapter-4-recognizing-measuring-identifiable-assets/4-10-intangible-assets){target="_blank"}
  - [PwC: Deferred Taxes in Business Combinations](https://viewpoint.pwc.com/dt/us/en/pwc/accounting_guides/income_taxes/income_taxes__16_US/chapter_10_business__US/104_identify_and_mea_US.html){target="_blank"}

- Additional References:
  - @flood2021wiley (Chapter 47)
  - @custodio2014mergers (M&A accounting and the diversification discount)
  - @stein2003agency (Agency costs in conglomerates) 
  - @rajan2000cost (Diversification discount and inefficient investment)


:::
